about: How Extended Mark reads the CommonMark 0.31.2 and GitHub 0.29 spec examples where it reads Markdown its own way. Each reading is the blocks Extended Mark gives, in the harness's form, and why. A reading marked "only": "prose" is Extended Mark's own syntax in a document; core's md.from, which reads Markdown as data, is held to CommonMark's output there.

commonmark-0.31.2.json#12.why: In prose, `\{` opens a hole (page 1, Prose), and `\{|}~` holds `|`, which is not code. A reader writes `\\{` for a literal brace. md.from reads Markdown with no holes and is held to CommonMark's output.

errors: [syntax.unexpected-character] `\` is not part of Extended Mark's code

commonmark-0.31.2.json#21.why: Extended Mark shows raw HTML as text and never runs it (page 1, Prose). The HTML block keeps CommonMark's extent, so the blocks around it are read as CommonMark reads them, and it is drawn as a paragraph of its own text.
